The test image shows tomato leaves with a distinct mosaic/mottling pattern — irregular pale greenish-white and darker green patches across the leaf surface. No distinct necrotic spots, no powdery coating, no water-soaked lesions. This strongly suggests a viral mosaic disease (CMV) or possibly Powdery Mildew.

Now I'll view one reference image for my top candidate, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.

The CMV reference shows severely distorted, narrow, filiform leaves — different from the test image which shows broad leaves with strong pale/dark green mottling. However, CMV can also present with mosaic mottling at different stages. The test image's pale greenish-white patches interleaved with darker green areas is a classic mosaic virus pattern, consistent with CMV on tomato.

The CMV reference didn't match perfectly (more distortion than mottling), but among all 18 classes, the mosaic/mottling pattern in the test image is most consistent with a viral mosaic disease, and CMV is the only mosaic virus in this class list.
